did_you_know.text: Did you know? David had been in Ziklag for only two days after returning from the battle with the Amalekites when the messenger arrived from the camp.
Did you know? The messenger expressed mourning by tearing his clothes and putting dust on his head; when he came to David, he fell to the ground and bowed down.
Did you know? The messenger reported to David not only the deaths of Saul and Jonathan, but also Israel’s defeat and the deaths of many of the people in battle.
Did you know? According to the messenger, Saul asked him to kill him because he was wounded and believed he would not survive.
Did you know? The messenger claimed that he had brought David Saul’s crown and armlet, royal symbols that had been on his body.
Did you know? David did not rejoice over the death of his rival; instead, he tore his clothes, and all his men did the same.
Did you know? David and his men mourned, wept, and fasted until evening for Saul, Jonathan, the people of the LORD, and the house of Israel who had fallen by the sword.
Did you know? David took the messenger’s claim that he had killed Saul very seriously and asked him how he had not been afraid to raise his hand against the LORD’s anointed.
Did you know? David ordered the people of Judah to be taught the use of the bow, and the lament for Saul and Jonathan is mentioned as being written in the Book of Jashar.

Did you know? In his lament, David asked that the news not be proclaimed in Gath or announced in the streets of Ashkelon, so that the daughters of the Philistines would not rejoice over Israel’s downfall.
